paths.description: Entry page and global template; selected for first-view hierarchy, navigation, preferences, performance, security, crawlability, and mobile layout.
Representative category/listing archetype; selected for search, list scanning, image cards, breadcrumbs, and mobile reflow.
Representative movie detail and primary download-choice journey; selected for content hierarchy, metadata, search form, and exposed resolution links. Binary downloads were not fetched.
Invalid-route recovery case; selected to assess HTTP/error recovery. It silently rendered the homepage rather than a clear not-found state.

findings.summary: The site ignores the user’s dark-color preference.
findings.evidence: The dark-mode capture is pixel-identical to light mode; the probe reports color-scheme normal and body background rgb(255,255,255) while the dark media query matches.
findings.suggestedFix: Declare color-scheme: light dark and use prefers-color-scheme or light-dark() for surfaces and text.

findings.summary: Essential text fails contrast even before stronger contrast preferences are applied.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse found multiple failures, including white text on #1b8cd8 at 3.62:1 and blue links on white at 4.06:1.
findings.suggestedFix: Use semantic color tokens that meet WCAG AA and add forced-colors/prefers-contrast adjustments.

findings.summary: Navigation changes are abrupt full-document swaps with no transition treatment.
findings.evidence: DOM/CSS inspection found no view-transition-name or @view-transition rules across the homepage, category, and detail templates.
findings.suggestedFix: Add cross-document View Transitions with a safe reduced-motion fallback for shared header/content changes.

findings.summary: Long listing pages provide no position-aware navigation or progress cue.
findings.evidence: The mobile homepage is 3171px tall and category is 2027px tall, while screenshots and CSS show only static chrome with no sticky/progress state.
findings.suggestedFix: Use a restrained sticky header or scroll progress affordance that reacts declaratively to scroll state.

findings.summary: Components only adapt through viewport rules, not their containing context.
findings.evidence: The platform probe found zero CSS container rules; authored CSS uses a single @media(max-width:600px) rule despite cards/components recurring in different contexts.
findings.suggestedFix: Give reusable cards/search/share components containment and size-aware @container rules where their composition changes.

findings.summary: Many primary text links are too small and tightly packed for touch.
findings.evidence: Mobile screenshots show 11–13px links packed into 15px rows; the focus probe confirms many link rectangles are only 15px high, although browser focus outlines remain visible.
findings.suggestedFix: Increase target padding/minimum target size and preserve visible :focus-visible styles.

findings.summary: An invalid URL silently renders the homepage instead of a clear recoverable 404 state.
findings.evidence: The invalid-route screenshot is indistinguishable from the homepage and provides no not-found message, correction, or search recovery.
findings.suggestedFix: Return HTTP 404 and render a concise not-found state with search, home, and relevant category links.

findings.summary: Cold-load LCP misses the good threshold in Lighthouse.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse measured LCP/FCP at 2.7s (performance 0.92), although the separate warm trace measured 1.985s with zero blocking time and CLS.
findings.suggestedFix: Remove redirect latency and prioritize the LCP path to keep cold-load LCP at or below 2.5s.

findings.summary: Redirects and render-blocking resources delay first content.
findings.evidence: The HAR recorded 301 and 302 redirects; Lighthouse estimates 850ms redirect savings, 990ms render-blocking savings, and flags weak cache lifetimes.
findings.suggestedFix: Link directly to the canonical host, inline or prioritize critical CSS, defer non-critical assets, and set durable cache headers.

findings.summary: The page ships avoidable unused CSS and third-party scripts.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse estimates 18KiB unused CSS; HAR and tracker evidence show analytics from Google Tag Manager, Histats, and Statcounter on a simple document.
findings.suggestedFix: Purge template CSS per archetype and remove or defer analytics that does not provide proportional user value.

findings.summary: The detail-page search field has no programmatic label and one tracking image lacks alt text.
findings.evidence: Detail DOM shows a placeholder-only text input with no label; image audit reports one missing-alt 1px tracker image.
findings.suggestedFix: Add a real label to search and hide decorative/tracking pixels from the accessibility tree with empty alt where retained.

findings.summary: Text and essential links do not meet WCAG contrast minimums.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse accessibility score is 0.68 and enumerates repeated red, blue, green, and white-on-blue failures from 3.62:1 to 4.09:1.
findings.suggestedFix: Replace hard-coded presentational colors with tested semantic tokens meeting at least 4.5:1 for normal text.

findings.summary: Page structure lacks a main landmark and has an illogical heading outline.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse flags no main landmark; the homepage has two H1 elements and only a footer landmark. Keyboard focus itself uses a visible browser outline.
findings.suggestedFix: Wrap primary content in main and create one descriptive H1 followed by ordered H2/H3 sections.

findings.summary: Body copy is cramped and unusually small across key mobile paths.
findings.evidence: Computed body text is 12px and much content is 11–13px; mobile screenshots show dense justified lines with minimal line spacing.
findings.suggestedFix: Use a fluid readable base size, comfortable line-height/measure, and avoid justification on narrow screens.

findings.summary: The viewport explicitly disables user zoom.
findings.evidence: Every inspected template declares width=device-width,initial-scale=1,user-scalable=no; Lighthouse fails meta-viewport.
findings.suggestedFix: Remove user-scalable=no and test 200–400% zoom/reflow while increasing small touch targets.

findings.summary: Assets and markup use fragile legacy patterns.
findings.evidence: Image audit found 20 of 24 images without dimensions and all 24 in legacy PNG/GIF formats; detail DOM uses obsolete font elements and inline presentational attributes.
findings.suggestedFix: Reserve image dimensions, modernize formats where useful, and replace font/align markup with semantic HTML and CSS.

findings.summary: Deprecated APIs and browser inspector issues are present.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse best-practices is 0.54, reports three deprecation warnings and an Inspector Issues failure.
findings.suggestedFix: Remove deprecated API usage, address DevTools Issues, and verify BFCache/platform diagnostics after cleanup.

findings.summary: Movie detail pages lack complete rich-entity and social preview metadata.
findings.evidence: The detail DOM has title, description, canonical and basic Open Graph text, but no JSON-LD movie schema and no og:image despite visible poster/content metadata.
findings.suggestedFix: Emit accurate Movie JSON-LD and complete Open Graph/Twitter image metadata matching the visible page.

findings.summary: HTTPS is used, but essential security headers are absent.
findings.evidence: Headers evidence reports no CSP, HSTS, X-Content-Type-Options, frame protection, Referrer-Policy, or Permissions-Policy.
findings.suggestedFix: Deploy a restrictive CSP, HSTS, nosniff, frame-ancestors, Referrer-Policy, and Permissions-Policy at the canonical origin.

findings.summary: Multiple analytics services load without an explained or minimized privacy posture.
findings.evidence: Tracker capture found six third-party origins and Google Tag Manager plus Histats and Statcounter; Lighthouse also observed two third-party cookies.
findings.suggestedFix: Remove redundant trackers, document purpose, minimize events, and gate non-essential analytics behind valid consent where required.

findings.summary: Browser-enforced defensive policies are not configured.
findings.evidence: The response lacks HSTS, clickjacking protection, Referrer-Policy, Permissions-Policy and CSP frame-ancestors; no exposed secrets were found.
findings.suggestedFix: Set defense-in-depth response policies and verify them on the final canonical response after redirects.

findings.summary: HTTP/not-found failure handling is misleading.
findings.evidence: A deliberately invalid route rendered normal homepage content with no error state, retry, search explanation, or status cue.
findings.suggestedFix: Return correct error status codes and provide actionable recovery content for 404, timeout, and upstream failure states.

findings.summary: The English language is declared, but layout CSS is built from physical directions and presentational alignment.
findings.evidence: DOM reports lang=en but no dir; stylesheet uses float:left, padding-left, margin-left and text-align:left rather than logical properties.
findings.suggestedFix: Declare direction intentionally and migrate reusable layout rules to logical inline/block properties.

findings.summary: Visible release dates are hard-coded in one English format.
findings.evidence: The detail page renders “26 Jun 2026”; static HTML/CSS inspection found no locale-aware formatting or machine-readable time element.
findings.suggestedFix: Emit machine-readable dates and format them with Intl.DateTimeFormat for the active locale.

findings.summary: Image delivery is not modernized or lazy below the fold.
findings.evidence: Image audit found 24/24 legacy PNG/GIF assets, 19 below-fold images without lazy loading, and 20 missing dimensions.
findings.suggestedFix: Use appropriate WebP/AVIF where beneficial, lazy-load below-fold assets, and set intrinsic dimensions.

findings.summary: The tracking footprint is disproportionate to this lightweight content page.
findings.evidence: The page transfers only about 71KB in 17 requests, yet contacts six third-party origins and loads three analytics products; there is no user-facing media on the homepage.
findings.suggestedFix: Remove duplicate analytics and defer any retained third-party code until it serves a demonstrated need.
